A Polish tourist, Mirka Czee, has shared screenshots of threats and abusive messages she received following her allegation of sexual assault against the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Faruk Umar Faruk. Amnesty International Nigeria on Tuesday condemned the threats against the tourist, saying she had received hundreds of death threats, including warnings that she would be tracked down and killed or harmed. The organisation said Czee had been subjected to round-the-clock attacks and cyberbullying since speaking out about the alleged incident at the Emir’s palace in Daura, Katsina State, on November 14. In a statement shared on its social media platforms, Amnesty said the messages warned the tourist to either withdraw her allegation or face death. “It is appalling that the foreign tourist that was allegedly sexually assaulted by the 92-year-old Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, has been receiving hundreds of death threats, including threats to track her wherever she is to kill or harm her,” the organisation said. Czee shared screenshots of some of the messages in an Instagram post on Monday, showing threats, insults and demands for her to delete the viral video of her encounter with the traditional ruler. Some of the messages accused her of deliberately trying to damage the Emir’s reputation, while others threatened her safety and warned her against returning to Nigeria. In one of the private messages, a user identified as Handel Benny accused the tourist of encouraging the alleged advances before publishing the video. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. You gave him the green light to continue after he continued, you rushed to social media to lament,” the message read. Other messages contained threats of violence, with one user warning Czee not to return to Africa, while another threatened harm against her and people from her country. The screenshots also showed several comments blaming the tourist for the alleged incident, accusing her of disrespecting Islam and Hausa traditions and questioning her reasons for publishing the recording. One private message also offered her $50,000 to remove the video, saying, “I will give you 50k$ if you can remove the video of Emir of Daura please.” Ex-Kaduna gov demands Daura emir’s suspension over sexual assault allegation Police deploy across Ibadan as NURTW threatens park takeover 2027: Police must be fair, neutral Amnesty said the attacks demonstrated why many rape cases went unreported in Nigeria, citing corruption, stigma and victim-blaming. It called on the Nigeria Police Force to provide necessary support to Czee and conduct an impartial and effective investigation into the allegation. “The Nigeria police must provide all necessary support to the survivor and act in line with their code of conduct, by carrying out impartial and effective investigation,” the organisation said. It also criticised what it described as the silence of the Katsina State Government, saying the response highlighted concerns about the prevalence of sexual abuse and the safety of women and girls. The development comes amid growing reactions to the allegation, which followed the circulation of a video appearing to show the Emir interacting with Czee during her visit to his palace. The tourist had alleged that the monarch held her hand, hugged her and kissed her cheek before touching her breasts without her consent. She said she repeatedly told him not to touch her, adding that she activated the recording function on her Meta smart glasses after becoming uncomfortable when he held her hand. Czee, who was born in the Czech Republic, said the incident happened on November 14, during a 30-day tour of Nigeria, but she waited until she had left the country before making the allegation public. The Daura Emirate Council said it was reviewing the viral footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated or artificially generated. Its spokesperson, Ibrahim Daura, said the council would issue an official statement after concluding the review. PUNCH Online could not independently confirm the allegation, while the Emir had yet to personally respond to it as of the time of filing this report.
